The important thing for me is that the architecture is there for communication for a short (in most cases) to medium amount of time. Communication is for me their primary use-case and with that they should be easy-ish to create; and it might not be important to continue to reference that particular version for long periods of time. But if it is easy to create/re-create/manipulate again in the future then it might have a longer life.

One of my biggest problems with architecture views is that it gets difficult to manage the amount of information in them and ensure they remain suitable for presentation on-screen. Different users also want more detailed views where I will often want the black-box view. I am sure there are way to render both from the same information. That being said, accessibility is an important part I am thinking about here.

There are aspects that cannot be generated such as a good graph layout to ease understanding. A good layout is very subjective, but can really help. I think it would be great if you could generate a diagram from the code, possibly using code annotations to identify what is relevant for this particular diagram and do the layout in a suitable graph editor. Regenerating the diagram from updated code could reuse the layout for existing components.
I believe where possible it is good to keep documentation such as architecture diagrams as close to the code as possible. Similar to how it's much better for doc comments to be right in the code instead of in separate files or even outside the repository. This helps update the documentation with updates to the code. Of course the diagram can't be in the source code, but some of it's inputs can be. For example you could annotate code to document that it belongs to some use case or some layer and then use that information to find all components of that use case / layer. It is important to be careful and not overload the diagram with technical details though so you would only want to annotate really important parts such as API endpoints or asynchronous buffer queues. I am not sure if there is a good place in code to annotate concepts such as queues. You will always want to manually add conceptual components to a diagram, but it can be helpful to automatically add components that are easy to recognize in the code such as endpoints.
